newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures reverse to end up, track NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures reverse to end up, track NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures rebounded from early lows to end Monday modestly higher and near last week's peaks of just over $1,790 mark on a fresh bout of short-covering on New York's surge.

Values were earlier pressured lower by Far East selling. But as Indonesian and Vietnamese selling thinned out in the afternoon, the market found support from rising New York arabicas to propel higher.
Benchmark July charged to an intraday high of $1,781 a tonne by late afternoon, up $24 on the day, after holding in the negative territory all morning.
By the close, the second-month position stood $18 up at $1,775.
New York's July contract hit a new contract high of 226.50 cents a lb after an earlier dip to below 219 cents triggered buy-stops.
Traders said a close above 225 cents is seen as technically constructive.
"Overall, New York is still in the bull phase," said one. The rally could accelerate on the first frost reports from Brazil, traders said. June and July are the frost danger months for Brazil.
Despite London's rise, traders said today's performance was barely spectacular.
An improved technical picture will emerge if July vaults over the immediate resistance levels at $1,800 and $1,820, the early March highs.
But the higher levels will inevitably attract scale-up Indonesian and possibly Vietnamese sales.
On the downside, London's July sees a strong support at $1,700.

Traders said activity was expected to remain thin in the coming days in view of a trade conference in Valencia, Spain, later this week and the approaching long holiday weekend in some European countries.
Last week's activity was also curtailed by several holidays in Europe.
Fundamentally, traders in Indonesia said although local supply was ample, there were expectations that it would be running out by the third quarter of this year.
"The season this year is expected to be shorter than last year," said one. Indonesia is the world's top robusta coffe grower.

In other news, German retail prices of roasted coffee would rise to 12 marks per 500-gram packet from 10 marks as roasters' price hike begin to hike, Kraft Jacobs Suchard said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
